title: Top Research Reports for S&P Global, Cloudflare & Canadian Natural
author: Mark Vickery
description: Zacks analysts published research on 16 major stocks and 2 microcaps on September 15, 2026. Key reports include S&P Global (neutral outlook despite strong recurring revenues and AI adoption), Cloudflare (balanced risk-reward with strong enterprise demand but valuation concerns), and Canadian Natural Resources (neutral stance due to commodity volatility and regulatory risks). Additional coverage includes Exelon, Nordson, Lamar Advertising, and others with mixed outlooks reflecting both growth opportunities and operational challenges.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Positive factors include recurring benchmark revenues, AI adoption, and margin improvements, but offset by elevated costs, sizable debt, and intense competition. Financial and execution risks limit near-term upside.

Strong enterprise demand and raised 2026 outlook are positive, but gross-margin compression, intense competition, macro uncertainty, workforce restructuring, and stretched valuation create balanced risk-reward profile.

Diversified portfolio and strong cash-flow generation are supported by low-cost assets, but significant oil sands exposure creates commodity volatility sensitivity and regulatory uncertainty. Pipeline constraints and ESG scrutiny limit upside.

Acquisition strategy and HVAC diversification provide growth opportunities, but persistent customer attrition, energy conversions, elevated commodity costs, and tariff uncertainty constrain organic growth and margins.

title: PPL Stock Underperforms Its Industry in the Past Month: How to Play?
author: Zacks.Com
description: PPL Corporation's shares fell 5.2% in the past month, underperforming its industry. While the company benefits from rising data center demand and plans $23 billion in regulated infrastructure investment through 2029, it trades at a premium valuation with below-industry ROE of 9.33% versus 11.4%, suggesting investors may wait for a better entry point. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: PPL has positive growth drivers including $23B infrastructure investment plan, 10.3% rate base CAGR, and rising data center demand. However, it trades at a premium (P/E 16.56X vs industry 14.7X), has below-industry ROE (9.33% vs 11.4%), and faces execution risks and competition. The Hold rating reflects balanced risks and opportunities.

title: Here's Why a Hold Strategy Is Apt for Southern Company Stock Now
author: Na
description: Southern Company (SO) is positioned to benefit from surging data center demand with over 17 GW of contracted load and an $81B capital plan supporting 9% rate-base growth. However, high capital requirements, equity dilution needs, rising borrowing costs, and regulatory risks present challenges. The stock has underperformed peers by 3% over the past 12 months, prompting analysts to recommend waiting for a better entry point.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While SO benefits from strong electricity demand growth (2.3% retail sales increase, 55% data center usage growth) and has substantial contracted demand (17+ GW pipeline, 3.2 GW OpenAI contract), significant headwinds exist including very high capital requirements ($6.76B invested in H1 2026), continued equity dilution needs ($1.1B through 2030), rising interest expenses, and regulatory cost-recovery risks. The stock's 3% decline over 12 months versus 13.1% gains for the Electric Power sub-industry suggests underperformance. Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating recommends waiting for better entry point.

title: Why Exelon (EXC) is a Great Dividend Stock Right Now
author: Na
description: Exelon (EXC), a Chicago-based utility company, offers an attractive dividend yield of 3.85%, above its industry average of 3.17%. With an annualized dividend of $1.68 (up 5% year-over-year) and a sustainable 60% payout ratio, the company is positioned for modest earnings growth with 2026 consensus estimates at $2.86 per share. Zacks rates EXC as a #2 Buy, making it a compelling option for income-focused investors seeking stable cash flow.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Exelon demonstrates strong dividend fundamentals with a yield of 3.85% above industry average, consistent dividend growth (5% year-over-year), a sustainable payout ratio of 60%, and expected earnings expansion in 2026. The company received a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating, indicating it is viewed as an attractive investment opportunity for income investors.

title: EXC vs. NEE: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
author: Na
description: In a comparison of two major utility stocks, Exelon (EXC) emerges as the more attractive option for value investors compared to NextEra Energy (NEE). EXC holds a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 15.24 and Value grade of B, while NEE has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 20.80 and Value grade of D. EXC's lower valuation metrics and stronger analyst outlook make it the preferred choice for value-focused investors.
